The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 01.12.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 01.12.2021 at about 2.00 p.m., when the petitioner was pedestrian and walking on the left side of road near railway bridge, West of Cord road, BBB layout, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02- JS-8119 came from behind at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, as a result he sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to BMC, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
3. It is further stated that the petitioner was working as a flower decorator and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
After the accident petitioner is not able to do his work as he was doing earlier and lost his income.

Petitioner has spent huge amount towards treatment, medicine,
conveyance etc., and requires more amount for his future treatment.

The accident has occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the offending motor cycle and hence 2nd respondent being the owner and 3rd respondent being the insurer of the offending motorcycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Inspite of service of summons respondents No.1 and 2 remained absent, hence they were placed exparte.

Kiran Kumar K.S vs Venkatappa on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87274426/
2 5.
After service of notice, the respondent No.3 appeared before the court by filing written statement contending that the petition is not maintainable either by law or on facts.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JS-8119.
However the liability if any is subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.

Non -compliance of section's 134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
This respondent specifically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident.
It is averred that the rider of the did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident, despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 01.12.2021 at about 2.00 p.m., near railway bridge of west of cord road, BBB layout, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JS- 8119 ?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and a witness as PW.2 and got marked 17 documents as per Ex.P1 to 17.
On the other hand, respondents have not led their evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the documents.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ...

In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 ...

Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 ...

As per final order  For the following:
 REASONS 10. Issues No.1:

As per the case of the petitioner, on 01.12.2021 at about 2.00 p.m., when the petitioner was pedestrian and walking on the left side of road near railway bridge, West of cord road, BBB layout, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing Kiran Kumar K.S vs Venkatappa on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87274426/
3 Reg.No.KA-02-JS-8119 came from behind at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, as a result he sustained grievous injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove his case,
got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R,
injured statement/FIS, Spot Mahazar, sketch, 133 notice and reply, IMV report, Wound certificate and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to P9.
11.
The 3rd respondent has not refuted the claim of the petitioners.
The evidence of PW-1 is not challenged.
The police filed charge sheet against the accused and the said charge sheet is also not disputed.
There is no evidence before this Tribunal on the side of the respondent that petitioner has falsely claimed compensation.

The sketch produced by the petitioner is marked at Ex.P4, it reveals that the side road divides as two part and both side there is pedestrian path, accident was occurred on road after two 2 feets of pedestrian path.
The accident place is shown as A, pedestrian path is shown as B.
The petitioner was walking on road and he admits in his cross examination he was not walking on pedestrian path, even there is a pedestrian path.

Hence, not only the rider of Motorcycle,
but the petitioner should have also taken utmost care while walking and when there is pedestrian path, he must walk on that path not on the road.

Hence, if the petitioner walked on pedestrian path,
then he could have avoid the accident.
At the same time, if the rider rode the motorcycle in a slow manner, then he could have applied the break and he could avoid the accident.
Hence, both are liable for cause of the accident.
The contribution of the petitioner is 20% since, he walked on the road, even there is existence of pedestrian path and accident occurred after 2 feets from the left side of the road.

The contribution of the rider for the accident is 80% since he rode the motor cylce in a rash manner without observing the pedestrian who was walking on the road, and he was unable to control his vehicle and dashed to the petitioner.
Apart from this Ex.P7 IMV report reveals that the accident was not due to any mechanical defect in the vehicle.
The chargesheet at Ex.P9 reveals that the petitioner sustained injuries due to accident.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-JS-8119.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
13. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as flower decorator and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and to prove the same, petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2021.
considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.2.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained left distal radius fracture and underwent ORIF with Kiran Kumar K.S vs Venkatappa on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87274426/
4 plate and screws on 01.12.2021.
On examination he found that the petitioner is facing difficulty in lifting weights and to carryon his profession as flower decorator and there is restriction on wrist movements.
He assessed 35% disability to the Left arm and 12% whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.2 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 10% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 30 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 01.12.2021.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P15 Adhaar card as 01.03.1990, the petitioner was aged 31 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 31 is 16 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.2,88,000/-(Rs.15,000x12x16x10/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

14. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
As per wound certificate produced at Ex.P8, the petitioner has sustained wrist cloud intraarticular volar barton fracture of distal radius and loss of teeth incisure and the doctor has opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
The Ex

. P10 Discharge Summary of Basavanagudi Medical Centre reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital on from 01.12.2021 to 03.12.2021 and underwent ORIF of left distal radius fracture with radius LCP.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
15. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.1,30,068/- at Ex.P11 and advance receipts marked at Ex.P12 to 14.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Further the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.1,30,068/- and he is entitled for the same.
16.
ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
Kiran Kumar K.S vs Venkatappa on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87274426/

5 As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 3 days, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.3,000/- under this head.

17. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.45,000/-
(15,000X3) under this head.

18. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 31 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 10% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.40,000/- on this head.
19. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
The doctor stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant which may cost Rs.60,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
Petitioner has to undergo surgery of removal of implant, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

20. Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:

 4. Conveyance, food and Rs. 3,000/-

6  nourishment, attendant  charges and other incidental  expenses.

5. Loss of income during laid up Rs. 45,000/-
 period  6. Loss of amenities in life/Life Rs. 40,000/-
 comforts and expectancy of life  7. Future medical expenses 30,000/-
 Total 5,86,068/-
 Less: 20% Contributory 1,17,214/-
 negligence of the petitioner Total compensation payable by Rs. 4,68,845/- the respondent No.3
In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,68,845/-.
21. Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding future medical expenses) is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
22. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-01.12.2021.
The breach of any of the policy conditions are not proved.
Hence, 1 st and 2nd respondent being the rider and owner and 3 rd respondent being the insurer of the offending motorcycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 3 rd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,68,845/-(Rupees Four lakhs sixty eight thousand eight hundred and forty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.4,38,845/-(excluding future expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.3 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount, 60% of the award amount shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
